newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-FRANCE LOOKING TO BOUNCE BACK AGAINST ITALY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRANCE LOOKING TO BOUNCE BACK AGAINST ITALY.

text.p: World Cup hosts France can take inspiration from Italy's performance against Brazil to end the dress rehearsal for the 1998 finals on a high note.
France seek to bounce back from defeat when they face the Italians in their closing Tournoi de France match at Parc des Princes on Wednesday.
Italy drew 3-3 with world champions Brazil in Lyon on Sunday in a superb match, the result handing the tournament to England, 1-0 winners against France the previous night in Montpellier.
But that defeat, too, could galvanise the French so they bow out of the Tournoi with a performance closer to their 1-1 draw with Brazil in the opening match in Lyon last Tuesday.

"Perhaps we need that (defeat) to relaunch ourselves," said AC Milan's Christophe Dugarry, one of several strikers whom coach Aime Jacquet is hoping can resolve France's problems of a dearth of goals.
"We're not satisfied, but sometimes a good defeat provokes a reaction which we would not have otherwise found," he said.
At Montpellier, France lost their first home match since November 1993 when a shock loss to Bulgaria in Paris denied them a place in the 1994 World Cup finals.

Jacquet's team, in the light of the peformances of their three rivals in the tournament who have scored 10 goals between them, are still World Cup outsiders, capable of very good football at times but very ineffective at others.
Cesare Maldini's Italians, meanwhile, have recovered their standing quickly after the faux pas against England, who beat them 2-0 in Nantes on Wednesday.
Jacquet is not, however, going to allow himself to be distracted by what is at stake in Wednesday's match: avoiding bottom place in the tournament.
He is determined to follow through his plan for the tournament and learn the lessons that will help him prepare France for a bid at winning their first World Cup in 12 months time.
"Our main problem at the moment is that we play a game without a thread. It's as if the French team had lost their fluidity. We play in bursts," Jacquet said.

Jacquet, having made eight changes from the Brazil match to face England, is expected to make a similar number of changes again, only back in the direction of the first match in which the French had a very good second half and equalised.
There is also the fatigue factor and Fabien Barthez's finger injury, sustained as Alan Shearer scored England's winner on Saturday, which could keep the Monaco goalkeeper out of the match.
Jacquet must also resolve the question of whether he can play Youri Djorkaeff and Zinedine Zidane together.
Djorkaeff feels better when they play together but is unhappy if asked to play up front, where Jacquet believes the Internazionale player is most effective, preferring a slightly deeper role.
France's top scorer with 14 goals, Djorkaeff is aware he cannot afford another unsatisfactory performance like Saturday's in Montpellier.
